purpose: City-specific cadastral-source research; findings are limited to observed first-party evidence.
name: Chishtian Sharif

queries.query: Chishtian Sharif Pakistan cadastral map parcel land records official
queries.result: First-party discovery identified the Punjab Land Records Authority and PULSE Punjab Urban Land Systems Enhancement map. PULSE exposes a Bahawalnagar cadastral-map layer and public map configuration, while the PLRA Cadastral Map page documents village-wise cadastral-map access.

queries.query: چشتیاں شریف پاکستان اراضی ریکارڈ نقشہ سرکاری
queries.result: Urdu-language first-party discovery identified the same Punjab government land-record and cadastral-map services. It supports provincial custodianship and a relevant official map route; it did not independently establish citywide parcel coverage.

registryEvidence.custodian: Punjab Land Records Authority / Government of Punjab; PULSE Punjab Urban Land Systems Enhancement public map service
registryEvidence.scopeNote: The official PLRA and PULSE interfaces evidence a relevant provincial cadastral/map custodian. The PULSE service includes a Bahawalnagar cadastral layer, which is the district containing Chishtian, but the tested response does not prove complete citywide coverage.

parcelDiscovery.source: PULSE / Punjab Cadastral Maps ArcGIS MapServer, Bahawalnagar layer 1
parcelDiscovery.crs: EPSG:4326 in retained sample; sourceSpatialReference EPSG:3857/Web Mercator

boundedResponse.requestedScope: Envelope 72.84-72.88 E, 29.77-29.82 N around Chishtian; spatialRelIntersects; resultRecordCount=3
boundedResponse.responseSummary: Three polygon features returned with native OBJECTID values 1032919, 1032920, and 1032921; response indicated exceededTransferLimit, so only the bounded three-feature sample was retained.

parcelDiscovery.note: The exact WUP point query returned zero features. This is not treated as citywide absence. The retained bounded sample is nearby but not claimed to be an exact-point hit; coordinates were not shifted. Native OBJECTID is preserved as the sole GeoJSON property identity.

requestsAndEndpointChecks.outcome: HTTP 200; current JavaScript/configuration inspected and followed to the Punjab Cadastral Maps ArcGIS service.
HTTP 200; official village-wise Cadastral Map page reached; it exposes district, tehsil, and village selection but no direct public vector URL in the page response.
HTTP 200; public application token endpoint returned a short-lived ArcGIS token without login. No credentials or private token was used.
HTTP 499 Token Required without the application token; the same metadata request succeeded with the public token supplied by the official PULSE application.

Authenticated official layer metadata returned Bahawalnagar polygon layer, sourceSpatialReference WKID 102100/latestWkid 3857, fields including OBJECTID, District, Dist_ID, Tehsil, Tehsil_ID, and QH. Only OBJECTID was requested for parcel geometry.
Anonymous-token point-intersects query at exact WUP point returned an empty FeatureCollection. This was recorded as an exact-point miss, not absence evidence.

Anonymous-token bounded envelope query around the city returned three full polygons with OBJECTID-only attributes and exceededTransferLimit=true. The sample was retained unchanged after converting output to GeoJSON EPSG:4326.

schemaAndCrs.geometryCrs: Source EPSG:3857/Web Mercator; retained GeoJSON response EPSG:4326

safeFieldAllowlist: stable native parcel identifier only if source-proven
scopeLimits: Exact WUP point [29.7965667323216, 72.8601389630638] was preserved in latitude/longitude order and not shifted.
The exact-point zero hit, bounded-envelope extent, transfer-limit flag, or any map/UI limitation is not evidence of citywide parcel absence.
The three retained polygons are a bounded nearby sample, not a complete city extract and not an exact-point match.
No owner, address, contact, titleholder, personal, tax/account, certificate, title, or other unsafe fields were requested or retained.
Packet completion is research completion only and is not source integration or admission.
uncertainty: The Bahawalnagar layer's district-wide polygon extent and relationship to the built-up Chishtian city boundary were not independently established.
OBJECTID is the service's native OID field, but long-term edit stability and cadastral legal identity were not separately documented by the public metadata.
Independent serial review is required before any adapter/runtime qualification.

qualification.reason: A safe bounded native OBJECTID-plus-polygon response was obtained from the official public map service; runtime qualification remains held pending serial review.
